en: The Sūtra on the Names of the Eight Great Auspicious Stūpas Spoken by the Buddha,
translated by the Tripitaka Master of the Western Heaven, Imperial Censor of the Third Order, Acting Minister of the Court of Imperial Entertainments,
and State Preceptor for Enlightened Teaching, Dharma-bhadra, by Imperial Decree.
At that time, the World-Honored One addressed the bhikṣus:
"I shall now proclaim the names of the eight great sacred stūpas.
Listen attentively, and I will speak for you."

What are these eight? They are: first, the Lumbinī Garden in the city of Kapilavastu, the place where the Buddha was born; second, beneath the Bodhi tree on the banks of the Nairañjanā River in the kingdom of Magadha, the place where the Buddha realized the fruit of the Way; third, the city of Vārāṇasī in the kingdom of Kāśi, the place where he turned the Great Wheel of Dharma; fourth, the Jeta Grove in the kingdom of Śrāvastī, the place where he manifested great supernormal powers; fifth, the city of Kuśinagara, the place where he descended from the Trāyastriṃśa Heaven; sixth, the city of Rājagṛha, the place where the śrāvakas questioned the Buddha regarding his lifespan for the sake of transforming and delivering beings; seventh, the city of Vaiśālī, the place of the sacred stūpa where he contemplated the duration of his life; and eighth, within the grove of śāla trees at the Great Twin Trees in the city of Kuśinagara, the place where he entered nirvāṇa.
"These are the eight great sacred stupas.
He spoke again in verse:
"In the city of Kapilavastu, the capital of King Śuddhodana, In the Lumbinī Garden, the place where the Buddha was born;"
On the banks of the Nairañjanā River in Magadha, he attained perfect enlightenment beneath the Bodhi tree;
in the city of Vārāṇasī in the kingdom of Kāśi, he turned the Great Wheel of Dharma twelve times;
within the Jeta Grove of the great city of Śrāvastī, he manifested supernatural powers that pervaded the three realms.
In the city of Kuśinagara in the kingdom of Kāśī, he descended from the palace of the Trāyastriṃśa gods;
in the great city of Rājagṛha, the Saṃgha made its division, as the Tathāgata skillfully transformed beings through his practice of compassion;
within the sacred stūpa in the great city of Vaiśālī, the Tathāgata reflected upon the duration of his lifespan.
In the powerful land of the city of Kuśinagara, he entered nirvāṇa between the twin śāla trees.

Regarding these eight great sacred stūpas, if there are brāhmaṇas, sons of good family, or daughters of good family who, having conceived great faith, construct stūpas and shrines, serve them, and make offerings, such persons will obtain great benefit, reap great rewards, and possess great renown; their fame will be universal, profound, and vast. Even the bhikṣus should likewise train themselves in this.

"Furthermore, monks, if there are sons or daughters of good family with pure faith who are able to make sincere offerings at these eight great stupas of spiritual power during their current lives, such persons will, upon the end of their lives, swiftly be reborn in the celestial realms."
At that time, the World-Honored One again addressed the bhikṣus:
"Listen attentively; I shall now speak of the kingdoms and cities where I have traveled and resided, as well as my duration in this world."
And he spoke in verse:
"Twenty-nine years he dwelt in the royal palace; Six years he practiced asceticism in the Snowy Mountains;
Five years he converted beings in the city of Rājagṛha; Four years he remained in the Viśākhavana grove."
He spent two years in retreat at Jāli Cave, and for twenty-three years he dwelt in Śrāvastī;
in Vaiśālī and the Deer Park, in Makula and the Trāyastriṃśa Heaven,
in Śiśumāra and Kauśāmbī, and on the mountain peak of the Jewel Stūpa as well as in the Great Wilds.
In the village of Veṇugrāma and in the city of Kapilavastu, the capital of King Śuddhodana—
having spent one year in each of these holy sites where the Tathāgata Śākya dwelt and moved about—
the Muni remained for eighty years in this manner before entering parinirvāṇa.
The Sūtra on the Names of the Eight Great Auspicious Stūpas Spoken by the Buddha.
